title: The ten-copy agent-contract replication idiom and its published span digest
content:
This repo's agent-facing contracts (plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md, 9 files, plus the shared Phase 4 preamble in plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md, 1 site -- 10 copies total) carry a shared idiom: a canonical rule passage stated byte-identically in all ten places, introduced by evidence.md's 'identical for every pipeline agent' heading convention. #40 found that idiom had ALREADY DRIFTED, 3 of 9 files, before this run touched it, and the drift direction was LOSS OF SPECIFIC MEASURED DETAIL under an unchanged heading -- the kind of drift a reader trusting the heading's promise would not notice. #40 shipped the property-not-implementation rule as a new byte-identical passage across all ten sites (span digest as merged at 7a052d3: 14b65c48479dfceefb780689adccfbd53656b21e; this value moves every time the block body changes and MUST NOT be trusted without re-computing it -- see the re-derivation command below) and, load-bearing for future edits to ANY of the ten sites, published the digest INSIDE the contract on a line immediately OUTSIDE the hashed span (a digest cannot cover itself), so a copy edited without updating its digest line fails a mechanical check loudly instead of shipping a stale, silently-trusted number. MECHANISM: the terminator line states its bounds EXPLICITLY -- from the '## The property, not the fix' heading to the end of THAT heading line, not to the next '## ' heading and not to end-of-file. Re-derivation command (script-file form; do not nest quotes on a command line, see the harness-defect note below): extract each of the ten spans by that exact bound, run `shasum` over each, and assert (a) exactly one distinct hash across all ten AND (b) count is 10 AND (c) the hash is not the empty-string digest (`da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709`). FOUR FALSE-ALARM READINGS ARE NAMED IN THE SHIPPED TEXT ITSELF, because three separate readers produced a false alarm before the bounds and digest were published, and each one is output-indistinguishable from real drift unless you know which discriminator rules it out: (1) ANCHORING THE TERMINATOR (adding a `$`/end-of-line anchor the design does not carry) makes extraction run to end-of-file in every copy -- since the trailing content differs per file, this produces TEN DISTINCT HASHES, output-identical to genuine ten-way drift; the discriminator is the digest match, not the group count. (2) STOPPING AT THE NEXT '## ' HEADING instead of the terminator's own end-of-line produces a HANDFUL OF GROUPS (files whose next heading differs group differently), also readable as partial drift. (3) READING TO END OF FILE (the general case of (1) when no anchor exists to notice) is the failure mode a naive extractor falls into by default; same ten-distinct-hashes signature. (4) TRIMMING THE SPAN'S TRAILING NEWLINE is the SUBTLEST of the four and the one #40's own reviewer (QA, Phase 4) found the other three false alarms did not cover: it gives a UNIFORM hash across all ten files -- so a naive 'do all ten agree?' check PASSES -- but that hash disagrees with the published digest (measured: with the terminator line's newline, the span hashes to 3f92ab1a58e985bd1708f9d340ce08921351f42c at that round's block text; trimmed, the same three files hash to 5abd3aa40baec08c67a39d3e5eb0af310ef9e8f5, later re-confirmed at a different block revision as 0cb16ae3bdb7bf634c0daedd5fa9a3a78765257a vs the shipped 14b65c48...). This is WHY the assertion compares the DIGEST, not merely the group count: 'ten agreeing hashes that are not the published one' means the trailing newline was trimmed, not that the block is safe. A FIFTH failure mode, recorded separately because it is a harness defect rather than a reading of the bounds: #40's own implementer's first census run printed ten DISTINCT hashes on a genuinely clean tree while the battery's own equivalent cell passed, and the cause was an unexamined shell-quoting layer (a `$` anchor added to the terminator regex in a nested-quote command line that neither the design nor the extraction function carried) -- re-run from a script FILE rather than nested shell quotes, it agreed with the battery. Recorded as the general rule about proving the mutation you applied is the mutation you meant, turned on your own harness: an unexamined quoting layer can manufacture catastrophic-looking drift that isn't there. GOVERNANCE LIMIT, STATED IN THE SHIPPED TEXT ITSELF: the rule this idiom guards is stated in FOUR places and hashed in only ONE. Beyond the ten block copies, review.schema.json's remediation description and secops.md's Style bullet and VETO reply template each restate the same rule outside the hashed span, and #40's QA panel proved BOTH of those two secops.md statements mutable (reworded) without reddening the digest or any other mechanical check -- they are re-read by hand or not at all. A coherent all-ten edit (every copy changed the same way, digest and canonical text updated together in one commit) defeats census, digest and byte-identity verbatim checks TOGETHER; the one control QA found that survives it is a role-claim-vs-observed-behaviour matrix (AC4.matrix in #40's verify-40.sh) that checks each agent's stated licence against what the shipped hook actually enforces for that role, for the nine agent roles -- it does NOT cover the orchestrator's own claim, which is checked by a single substring match ('no SubagentStop at all'). A future editor of any of the ten sites must re-run the digest AND re-apply the two secops.md worked cases by hand; the mechanical check alone is not sufficient evidence of correctness.

CORROBORATED AT #21 (merged to main as cab267f, PR #81), A FOURTH CONFIRMING INSTANCE OF THE DIGEST HOLDING ACROSS A REAL EDIT: #21 touched FOUR of the ten replicated-span files (agents/ba.md, agents/dev.md, agents/secops.md, commands/pipeline.md) plus one file that does not carry the span (scripts/config-doctor.mjs), all with edits SITED FAR OUTSIDE each file's own span (ba.md 23-37 vs the edit at 61-63; dev.md 26-40 vs 77; secops.md 24-38 vs 122; pipeline.md 770-784 vs 125). Re-measured post-merge: all ten files carrying the span still hash to the SAME published digest, `14b65c48479dfceefb780689adccfbd53656b21e`, unchanged from #40. #21's own reviewer (DBA) additionally ran a NON-ZERO CONTROL specific to this edit: a one-character edit inside one file's span still yields a DIFFERENT hash, confirming the ten-way equality is not a harness that hashes nothing. This is now the SECOND independent post-#40 run (after #63/#61) to leave the digest unchanged while editing 4-5 of the ten carrying files outside their spans -- useful precedent for a future editor deciding whether an edit is 'far enough outside the span' to trust without re-running the digest by hand: re-run it anyway, but the pattern of untouched digests across genuinely unrelated edits is itself evidence the bounds are being read correctly by successive editors, not merely luck.

A SECOND, DISTINCT REPLICATED SPAN NOW EXISTS, ADDED AT #19 (merged to main as c337579, PR #86), AND IT IS NOT THE SAME IDIOM DESCRIBED ABOVE -- it has a different member count, a different heading, and a different terminator, and confusing it with the first span was independently attempted by three readers during #19 itself. WHERE: the nine agent-contract files (plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md -- ba, dba, design, dev, devops, librarian, qa, secops, art-director) each carry a block headed `## Phase 4 tracked-write isolation`. commands/pipeline.md carries a COMPRESSED RESTATEMENT of the same rule inline, in the body of its `## Phase 4: Peer Review Panel` section, under NO heading of its own -- it is NOT byte-identical to the nine-copy block and is NOT one of the counted copies: the new idiom is NINE files, not ten. Measured: the nine-copy block is 7583 bytes: pipeline.md's paragraph is a single 2651-byte line (`shasum` of that line alone, same normalization as below: `34db7dc2b5c75793d4159a2651ed2d26984e927f`), and it reached its own new wording in this same commit, separately from the nine-copy block, because it independently carried the other half of #19's defect (the disqualified 'stat the components' phrasing). It moves on its own; do not hash it expecting it to agree with the nine, and do not read 'restatement' as 'copy'. BOUNDS: the span runs from the `## Phase 4 tracked-write isolation` heading to END OF FILE in each of the nine agent contracts (there is no following `## ` heading to stop at; this heading is the last section in every one of the nine files) -- a materially different bound from the first span, which stops at end-of-heading-line, not end-of-file. TERMINATOR: the span's own closing sentence is 'These paragraphs are one block, copied byte-for-byte into all nine agent contracts. If two copies disagree, the disagreement is the defect, not a variation.' -- it ends on 'copied byte-for-byte' and NEVER on 'replicated verbatim', which is the first span's terminator phrase and belongs only to that block. A reader who greps for 'replicated verbatim' to bound or verify THIS block will match nothing in it and either falsely conclude it is unguarded or bound it wrong. DIGEST, RE-DERIVED DIRECTLY FROM THE TREE AT c337579 rather than trusted from any prior artifact: `for f in plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md; do sed -n '/^## Phase 4 tracked-write isolation$/,$p' "$f" | shasum; done | sort | uniq -c` prints one group, count 9, hash `dca27f7affc21fba08763e1eb3c9e605644de004`. EXTRACTION NORMALIZATION, STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE FIRST SPAN'S OWN ENTRY ABOVE DOCUMENTS TRAILING-NEWLINE TRIMMING AS THE SUBTLEST FALSE ALARM: the span above is extracted WITH its trailing newline kept (sed's range print includes the file's own final newline, since every one of the nine files ends in one) -- stripping that trailing newline before hashing (`printf '%s'` instead of `printf '%s\n'`, or piping through a construct that eats the last `\n`) changes the digest to `b22c1a389d220d085efc9843411ed9384434de16`, uniform across all nine but NOT the value above: the same 'nine agrees but disagrees with the published number' signature the first span's entry warns about. Both the old ten-file span (heading-line-bounded, terminated on 'replicated verbatim') and the new nine-file span (end-of-file-bounded, terminated on 'copied byte-for-byte') were re-measured together in this pass, same normalization (trailing newline kept) for both: the OLD span still hashes to `14b65c48479dfceefb780689adccfbd53656b21e` across all ten files, unchanged since #40/#21 and confirming the first span was untouched by #19's edit. NO DIGEST IS PUBLISHED INSIDE THE NEW BLOCK ITSELF (unlike the first span, which states its own hash inline on the line immediately after its terminator), and NO MECHANICAL TEST checks the nine copies against each other or against this recorded value as of c337579 -- both BA (peer-review.ba.json, C1) and Dev (impl-report.json) filed knowledge-store drift claims during #19 flagging exactly this gap, and #19's own record notes a test is tracked separately (#76) rather than shipped with the block. PROVENANCE NOTE ON THE REVIEWERS' OWN RECORDED DIGESTS: BA's peer-review shard recorded `151327c8aa961a47cfd574c95904d8dacd82739a` and Dev's impl report recorded `e10ca5c2d033a35967a71428fcc732d5f015e2b6` for this same nine-file span -- NEITHER reproduces against the merged c337579 tree (re-run here, both BA's own awk-based command and Dev's own sed-plus-trailing-whitespace-trim command now print `dca27f7affc21fba08763e1eb3c9e605644de004` like every other extraction tried in this pass). Read as: both were captured against an in-flight revision of the block during the fix round, before the final wording landed, and neither figure should be treated as describing the shipped text. The published digest of record for the shipped block is the one re-derived directly against c337579 in this entry, `dca27f7affc21fba08763e1eb3c9e605644de004`, not either reviewer's in-round number. A future editor of any of the nine `## Phase 4 tracked-write isolation` copies (or of pipeline.md's uncounted inline restatement) should re-run the extraction command above before trusting either published hash, and should not assume the two spans' bounding rules are interchangeable: same file set apart from pipeline.md's inline copy, different heading, different end bound, different terminator phrase, different hash.
